newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, China seal new ties with Li Peng visit.
newsitem.headline: Russia, China seal new ties with Li Peng visit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin expects Chinese President Jiang Zemin to visit Moscow in April for talks to set the seal on a new level of relations between the two giant states, the Kremlin said on Friday.

The visit was agreed during a 50-minute meeting between Yeltsin and Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng, the Russian president's first with a foreign leader since returning to work this week after a heart bypass operation on November 5.
"I am very pleased with the course of events," Yeltsin, thinner but apparently healthier, told officials in brief remarks broadcast on Russian television.
Li later met Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and they agreed to meet each other twice a year to monitor progress on building up trade and diplomatic relations.
They also signed several deals ranging from the supply of Russian warplanes and building a nuclear power plant in China's Jiangsu province to an accord between the two central banks.
"We laid a good foundation for the next century and the next millennium," Chernomyrdin told reporters.

A joint communique said: "The establishment of an equal partnership of trust between Russia and China, aimed at strategic cooperation in the 21st century, meets the fundamental interests of the people of both countries."
Moscow and Beijing, once bitter rivals for leadership of the communist world, have been building steadily warmer and closer ties since Soviet communism began to unravel a decade ago.
For Russia, democracy has been accompanied by poverty and Moscow sees China as a huge market for its struggling industry.

"We have the desire and the possibility to work, two great states have huge potential for cooperation in every field," RIA news agency quoted Chernomyrdin saying. "Our task is to make use of these possibilities, which we want to do and will do."
Li was quoted as saying that his twice-yearly meetings with Chernomyrdin would "promote trade, economic and technical cooperation between our two countries."

Kremlin press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Jiang, together with leaders of the former Soviet republics of Tajikistan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, would sign an accord in April reducing forces on their borders.

China and the former Soviet Union clashed along their border in the 1960s. Disputes over border demarcation were for the most part resolved in 1991 and Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin, who visited China last April, had promised to finalise the issue next year.
Russia's desire to develop close links with China has followed NATO's plans to expand eastwards by admitting Moscow's Cold War allies in Eastern Europe as members of the alliance.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Li agreed that the future political map of the globe should be "a multi-pole world which is not divided into leaders and those who are being led."

Yeltsin has said more than once that he seeks a strategic partnership between Russia and China. But he has ruled out a revival of the close political and military alliance that existed between Moscow and Beijing in 1950s.
The joint communique said the two countries hoped to see bilateral annual trade at $20 billion in the next few years. Trade was $6.38 billion in the first nine months of this year.
Russian Defence Industry Minister Zinovy Pak told Interfax the two delegations signed a deal on the supply of Russian Sukhoi Su-27 fighters to China. He gave no details.
